agent.name: Cross-entropy method
agent.summary: Searches linear threshold policies by the cross-entropy method: sample a population, keep the elite, refit, repeat.

agent.name: LQR bang-bang
agent.summary: Pushes in the direction of the LQR force about the origin, from autodiff Jacobians of the model: a two-action baseline.

agent.name: Energy swing-up + LQR
agent.summary: Pumps the pendulum’s energy to the upright’s, then balances it with an LQR gain from autodiff Jacobians of the model.

agent.name: Deep Q-network
agent.summary: A multilayer perceptron Q(o, ·) trained by Adam on Huber TD errors from an experience-replay buffer, with a target network and ε-greedy exploration.

agent.name: ε-greedy
agent.summary: The best empirical mean, or with probability ε a uniformly random arm (optionally decaying as cK/t).

agent.name: EXP3
agent.summary: Exponential weights on importance-weighted rewards, mixed with uniform exploration: for adversarial arms.

agent.name: Expected SARSA
agent.summary: TD control bootstrapping from the expected action value under the ε-greedy policy.

agent.name: Explore then commit
agent.summary: Pulls every arm m times in turn, then the best empirical mean for ever.

agent.name: KL-UCB
agent.summary: Pulls the arm with the largest KL upper confidence bound; asymptotically optimal for Bernoulli arms.

agent.name: LinUCB
agent.summary: Ridge regression on the arms’ features plus an exploration bonus α‖x‖ in the inverse design matrix.

agent.name: Linear Thompson sampling
agent.summary: Draws θ from the ridge posterior N(θ̂, v²V⁻¹) and pulls the arm whose features score highest under it.

agent.name: Monte Carlo control
agent.summary: First-visit Monte Carlo control with an ε-soft policy: action values average the returns that followed.

agent.name: n-step SARSA
agent.summary: SARSA with n-step returns: n rewards, then the value of the action taken n steps later.

agent.name: Policy iteration (planner)
agent.summary: Solves the environment’s tabular model by policy iteration, then acts greedily on the optimal Q.

agent.name: Q-learning
agent.summary: ε-greedy Q-learning: one off-policy TD update towards r + γ max Q per transition.

agent.name: Random agent
agent.summary: Acts uniformly at random over the legal actions or the action domain and learns nothing: the baseline.

agent.name: REINFORCE
agent.summary: A tabular softmax policy improved by the score-function gradient of each episode’s returns.

agent.name: SARSA
agent.summary: On-policy TD control: each update bootstraps from the value of the action actually taken next.

agent.name: One-step TD control
agent.summary: Q-learning, SARSA or expected SARSA by `method`: ε-greedy TD control on discrete observations.

agent.name: TD(0) prediction
agent.summary: Follows a fixed policy (default uniformly random) and learns its state values by one-step TD updates.

agent.name: Thompson sampling (Bernoulli)
agent.summary: Draws each arm’s success probability from its Beta posterior and pulls the largest draw.

agent.name: Thompson sampling (Gaussian)
agent.summary: Draws each arm’s mean from its Gaussian posterior (known noise) and pulls the largest draw.

agent.name: UCB1
agent.summary: Pulls the arm with the largest upper confidence bound, the mean plus √(c ln t / n).

agent.name: Uniform (round robin)
agent.summary: Pulls the arms in turn, an A/B/n test: linear regret, the baseline of the bandit policies.

agent.name: Value iteration (planner)
agent.summary: Solves the environment’s tabular model by value iteration, then acts greedily on Q*: the optimal baseline.

algorithm.name: PID control loop
algorithm.summary: A discrete PID controller around a SISO plant, with a filtered derivative, actuator limits and anti-windup.

algorithm.name: Map iteration
algorithm.summary: x_{n+1} = f(x_n) for a map of the line or of ℝᵈ, one iterate per step.

algorithm.name: Adaptive BDF
algorithm.summary: Variable-order (1–5), variable-step backward differentiation formulae (NDF) for stiff problems, as scipy BDF.

algorithm.name: Backward differentiation formula
algorithm.summary: The BDF methods of order 1 to 3 for stiff problems.

algorithm.name: Dormand–Prince
algorithm.summary: The adaptive 5(4) embedded Runge–Kutta pair with error-controlled step sizes.

algorithm.name: Explicit Runge–Kutta
algorithm.summary: A fixed-step explicit Runge–Kutta method from a Butcher tableau (Euler, Heun, midpoint, RK4).

algorithm.name: Symplectic integrator
algorithm.summary: Symplectic Euler, leapfrog and higher-order splittings for separable Hamiltonians.

algorithm.name: Density of a scalar SDE
algorithm.summary: The density of dX = a(X) dt + σ(X) dW evolved by its Fokker–Planck equation.

algorithm.name: Fokker–Planck equation
algorithm.summary: p_t = −(ap)_x + (Dp)_xx in conservative form with reflecting ends.

algorithm.name: Heat equation
algorithm.summary: u_t = D u_xx by the method of lines: FTCS, implicit Euler or Crank–Nicolson.

algorithm.name: Transport equation
algorithm.summary: u_t + c u_x = 0 by upwind, Lax–Friedrichs or Lax–Wendroff differences.

algorithm.name: Wave equation
algorithm.summary: u_tt = c² u_xx by the leapfrog scheme.

algorithm.name: Blelloch scan
algorithm.summary: The work-efficient parallel prefix: an up-sweep of partial reductions, then a down-sweep of prefixes.

algorithm.name: Hillis–Steele scan
algorithm.summary: The inclusive parallel prefix in ⌈log₂ n⌉ rounds, each position combining with the one 2^t before it.

algorithm.name: DDIM sampling
algorithm.summary: Deterministic (η = 0) or partly stochastic sampling on a subsequence of the noise levels.

algorithm.name: Denoiser training
algorithm.summary: Minibatch MSE between predicted and true noise at a random level per point (the simplified DDPM loss).

algorithm.name: Forward noising chain
algorithm.summary: x_t = √αₜ x_{t−1} + √βₜ ε, one step per noise level, until x_T is nearly N(0, I).

algorithm.name: Probability-flow ODE sampler
algorithm.summary: The deterministic ODE dx = [f − ½g²∇log p_t] dt with the same marginals as the forward SDE.

algorithm.name: Reverse-time SDE sampler
algorithm.summary: Euler–Maruyama on dx = [f − g²∇log p_t] dt + g dw̄, backwards in time.

algorithm.name: JEM training
algorithm.summary: Cross-entropy plus persistent contrastive divergence on the energy −logsumexp of the logits.

algorithm.name: GAN training
algorithm.summary: Alternating discriminator and generator updates under the minimax, non-saturating, WGAN-GP or hinge game.

algorithm.name: Edmonds–Karp
algorithm.summary: Maximum flow by shortest augmenting paths.

algorithm.name: Minimum-cost flow
algorithm.summary: Minimum-cost flow by successive shortest paths with potentials.

algorithm.name: Policy iteration
algorithm.summary: Evaluate the policy exactly, then improve it greedily, until it stops changing.

algorithm.name: Value iteration
algorithm.summary: Bellman optimality backups V ← max_a [r + γ P V] until the residual is small.

algorithm.name: Bayes point machine (EP)
algorithm.summary: A Gaussian posterior over linear-classifier weights by expectation propagation, one site per example.

algorithm.name: CAVI for a Gaussian with unknown mean and precision
algorithm.summary: Coordinate ascent on q(μ)q(τ); each update raises the ELBO.

algorithm.name: Chain sum–product
algorithm.summary: Sum–product (or max–product) on a chain-shaped factor graph.

algorithm.name: Enumeration
algorithm.summary: Exact inference by enumerating every assignment.

algorithm.name: Expectation propagation over a linear-Gaussian model
Variational Bayesian Gaussian mixture
algorithm.summary: CAVI on q(π) q(μ, Λ) q(z) for a Gaussian mixture; the ELBO never decreases.

algorithm.name: TrueSkill by expectation propagation
algorithm.summary: Skills from a sequence of matches, by EP over the match factor graphs.

algorithm.name: Template CRF training
algorithm.summary: L-BFGS, OWL-QN (L1 + L2), SGD or Adam on the regularised conditional log-likelihood.

algorithm.name: Gibbs sampling on a factor graph
Langevin on a batch of particles
LDA by collapsed Gibbs sampling
algorithm.summary: Resamples each token’s topic from its full conditional with θ and φ integrated out; one sweep per step.

algorithm.name: Blahut–Arimoto (capacity)
algorithm.summary: Alternating maximisation of I(X; Y) over the input distribution, with upper and lower bounds.

algorithm.name: Huffman coding
algorithm.summary: Pop the D least-weight roots off a priority queue, join them under a new node and push it back, until one tree remains; binary or D-ary, with a tie-breaking rule.

algorithm.name: Pool adjacent violators
algorithm.summary: Add points one at a time and pool the last two blocks while they violate the order.

algorithm.name: GPLVM fit
algorithm.summary: L-BFGS on the latent positions and kernel hyperparameters of a GPLVM, maximising the log posterior.

algorithm.name: RVM by fast marginal-likelihood maximisation
algorithm.summary: Tipping and Faul: add, re-estimate or delete one basis function (or update β) per step by the largest gain.

algorithm.name: RVM by re-estimation
algorithm.summary: Tipping (2001): αᵢ ← γᵢ/μᵢ² and β ← (N − Σγ)/‖y − Φμ‖² for all basis functions per step, with pruning.

algorithm.name: Sparse GP fit by L-BFGS
algorithm.summary: L-BFGS on the sparse objective (the VFE bound, or FITC/DTC/SoR evidence) over log θ, log σ² and Z.

algorithm.name: Sparse GP by greedy inducing-point selection
algorithm.summary: Add the candidate training input that most raises the sparse objective, one per step, optionally re-optimising.

algorithm.name: Backfitting
algorithm.summary: Cycle over the terms of an additive model, smoothing the partial residuals of each in turn.

algorithm.name: Explainable boosting machine
algorithm.summary: Cyclic gradient boosting of one binned shape function per feature, with a small learning rate.

algorithm.name: GAM by Adam
algorithm.summary: Adam on the penalised deviance per observation, full batch, with the gradient by autodiff.

algorithm.name: GAM by backfitting
algorithm.summary: Backfitting with local scoring: one sweep of penalised smoothers over the terms per step.

algorithm.name: GAM by gradient descent
algorithm.summary: Gradient descent on the penalised deviance per observation, with the gradient by autodiff.

algorithm.name: GAM by L-BFGS
algorithm.summary: L-BFGS with a strong Wolfe line search on the penalised deviance per observation, by autodiff.

algorithm.name: GAM by penalised IRLS
algorithm.summary: Penalised IRLS on a GAM problem: weighted ridge-type solves on the working response, with step halving.

algorithm.name: GAM by minibatch SGD
algorithm.summary: Stochastic gradient descent on minibatch estimates of the penalised deviance, by autodiff.

algorithm.name: Negative binomial GLM by alternation
algorithm.summary: Alternate IRLS for the coefficients and a one-dimensional MLE for the dispersion θ.

algorithm.name: Iteratively reweighted least squares
algorithm.summary: Fisher scoring for a GLM as weighted least squares on the working response, optionally penalised.

algorithm.name: Pegasos
algorithm.summary: Stochastic subgradient descent on the primal SVM objective.

algorithm.name: Sequential minimal optimisation
algorithm.summary: Update two dual variables per step in closed form.

algorithm.name: Perceptron
algorithm.summary: Visit one example per step and add yx to the weights when it is misclassified; the averaged weights too.

algorithm.name: Mixture density network training by Adam
algorithm.summary: Minibatch Adam on the mixture negative log-likelihood of an MLP with a Gaussian-mixture head (or the squared error of the same body).

algorithm.name: EM for a mixture of linear experts
algorithm.summary: E-step responsibilities from the gate and each expert’s likelihood; M-step weighted least squares (or IRLS) per expert and a soft-target logistic refit of the gate, flat or hierarchical.

algorithm.name: Mixture-of-experts training by Adam
algorithm.summary: Minibatch Adam on the data loss plus the load-balancing, importance and router z auxiliary losses.

algorithm.name: Random forest growth
algorithm.summary: One tree per step on a bootstrap sample with random feature subsets.

algorithm.name: AdaBoost
algorithm.summary: One weak learner per step on reweighted examples; the vote weight grows with its accuracy.

algorithm.name: Gradient boosting
algorithm.summary: One regression tree per step fitted to the negative gradient of the loss, added with shrinkage.

algorithm.name: Decision-tree growth
algorithm.summary: Split one node per step by the best impurity decrease, in depth-, breadth- or best-first order.

algorithm.name: FlashAttention forward pass
algorithm.summary: Attention one tile of queries × keys at a time, folding each into a running maximum, normaliser and output.

algorithm.name: Beam search
algorithm.summary: Keep the B best partial sequences by length-penalised log-probability, recording the search tree.

algorithm.name: Greedy decoding
algorithm.summary: Append the most probable next token, one token per step.

algorithm.name: Sampling with temperature, top-k, top-p and repetition penalty
algorithm.summary: Draw each next token from the processed next-token distribution.

algorithm.name: Speculative decoding
algorithm.summary: Draft γ tokens with a small model, verify them with the target, keep the target’s distribution exactly.

algorithm.name: Adversarial training
algorithm.summary: Alternating gradient steps on a critic and a generator, k critic steps per generator step.

algorithm.name: Persistent contrastive divergence
algorithm.summary: Energy-based-model training with Langevin negatives from a replay buffer, plus an optional supervised term.

algorithm.name: Full-batch training (L-BFGS)
algorithm.summary: A network trained on the whole set by a vector method (L-BFGS by default): the parameter tree raveled to θ, the loss and its gradient on all the data.

algorithm.name: Training loop
algorithm.summary: Minibatch training of a network: forward, loss, gradients and an optimiser update per step.

algorithm.name: Gauss–Seidel and SOR
algorithm.summary: Sweeps that use each updated component at once, with optional over-relaxation ω.

algorithm.name: Gram–Schmidt
algorithm.summary: Orthonormalise the columns one at a time, classical or modified; after n steps A = QR.

algorithm.name: Householder QR
algorithm.summary: One reflector per column maps it onto a multiple of e₁ below the diagonal; QR = A throughout.

algorithm.name: Jacobi iteration
algorithm.summary: x ← D⁻¹(b − (L + U)x), every component from the previous iterate.

algorithm.name: Power iteration
algorithm.summary: v ← Av/‖Av‖ with the Rayleigh quotient as the eigenvalue estimate; inverse iteration with a shift.

algorithm.name: Continuation
algorithm.summary: Natural-parameter continuation from an easy problem to the target, with a Newton corrector.

algorithm.name: Linear conjugate gradient
algorithm.summary: Conjugate gradient for Ax = b with A symmetric positive definite.

algorithm.name: OWL-QN
algorithm.summary: L-BFGS for f(x) + C‖x‖₁: pseudo-gradient, orthant-projected direction and backtracking along the projected path.

algorithm.name: EMD sifting
algorithm.summary: The sifting iterations that extract one intrinsic mode function.

algorithm.name: Variational mode decomposition
algorithm.summary: ADMM sweeps that fit K narrow-band modes and their centre frequencies together, in the Fourier domain.

algorithm.name: Least mean squares (LMS)
algorithm.summary: An adaptive FIR filter that takes one stochastic-gradient step on the squared error per sample.

algorithm.name: Normalised LMS
algorithm.summary: LMS with each step divided by the regressor's energy, so the step size does not depend on the input scale.

algorithm.name: Recursive least squares (RLS)
algorithm.summary: An adaptive FIR filter that keeps the exact exponentially weighted least-squares taps, updated per sample.

algorithm.name: LTI simulation
algorithm.summary: Steps a discrete LTI system x[k+1] = A x[k] + B u[k] through an input sequence.

algorithm.name: Liang's pattern matching
algorithm.summary: Hyphenate a word by patterns: each step applies the patterns starting at one position of .word., keeping the largest digit per gap; odd digits hyphenate.

algorithm.name: PATGEN pattern learning
algorithm.summary: Learn hyphenation patterns level by level from hyphenated words: each step is one pass (a level and a pattern length) keeping candidates with good·w₊ − bad·w₋ ≥ threshold.

algorithm.name: Tokeniser training through a pipeline
algorithm.summary: BPE or WordPiece merges, or unigram pruning rounds, on the pre-tokens the pipeline cuts; a merge or round per step.

algorithm.name: Byte-pair encoding training
algorithm.summary: Merge the most frequent adjacent symbol pair, one merge per step, recording the merge and its count.

algorithm.name: Unigram language-model tokeniser training
algorithm.summary: EM on piece probabilities, then prune the pieces whose removal lowers the likelihood least; a round per step.

algorithm.name: WordPiece training
algorithm.summary: Merge the pair with the highest score c_ab / (c_a c_b) (or likelihood gain), one merge per step.

algorithm.name: ARMA fit by maximum likelihood
algorithm.summary: Nelder–Mead on the exact Gaussian ARMA likelihood over partial-autocorrelation coordinates.

algorithm.name: Exponential smoothing fit
algorithm.summary: Nelder–Mead on the one-step SSE over logit coordinates of the smoothing parameters.

algorithm.name: Seasonal ARIMA fit by maximum likelihood
algorithm.summary: Nelder–Mead on the exact likelihood of the differenced series under the expanded seasonal ARMA.

algorithm.name: EM for a linear-Gaussian state-space model
algorithm.summary: RTS-smoother E-step and closed-form M-step; the log-likelihood never decreases.

algorithm.name: Agglomerative clustering
algorithm.summary: Merge the two closest clusters per step under a linkage rule.

algorithm.name: EM for a Gaussian mixture
algorithm.summary: E-step responsibilities, M-step weights, means and covariances; the log-likelihood never decreases.

algorithm.name: Lloyd's k-means
algorithm.summary: Assign each point to its nearest centroid, then move each centroid to its cluster mean.

algorithm.name: SMACOF
algorithm.summary: Majorisation steps (the Guttman transform) that never increase metric stress.

algorithm.name: t-SNE
algorithm.summary: Gradient steps with gains and early exaggeration on the KL divergence between neighbour distributions.

algorithm.name: UMAP layout
algorithm.summary: One epoch of attractive edge samples and negative samples per step.

bijector.name: chain
bijector.summary: The composition of bijectors, applied left to right.

bijector.name: ordered
bijector.summary: Maps ℝᴷ onto increasing vectors: the first entry, then positive gaps (ordinal thresholds).

dataset.name: Anscombe's quartet
dataset.summary: Four small datasets with the same summary statistics and different shapes.

dataset.name: Coal-mining disasters
dataset.summary: Yearly counts of British coal-mining disasters, 1851–1962.

dataset.name: Fonts
dataset.summary: Capital-letter outlines of 66 fonts in dense correspondence, one row per font.

dataset.name: Moby hyphenation
dataset.summary: Common English words with dictionary hyphenation points (Moby Hyphenator, public domain), split into train and test words.

dataset.name: Iris
dataset.summary: Fisher's iris measurements: 150 flowers, four features, three species.

dataset.name: Old Faithful
dataset.summary: Eruption durations and waiting times of the Old Faithful geyser.

dataset.name: Autoregressive process
dataset.summary: An AR(2) with a conjugate pole pair of chosen radius and frequency (or any AR(p)), with its analytic PSD.

dataset.name: ARMA process
dataset.summary: An ARMA(2, 2) with a spectral peak from its poles and a notch from its zeros, with its analytic PSD.

dataset.name: Coupled pair of processes
dataset.summary: x an AR(2) and y a delayed low-pass of x plus independent noise, with known cross-spectrum and coherence.

dataset.name: Sinusoids in white noise
dataset.summary: Two sinusoids in white noise: a line spectrum on a flat floor.

dataset.name: Unevenly sampled sinusoid
dataset.summary: A sinusoid observed at random, gapped or nightly-and-seasonal times, with per-sample noise.

dataset.name: Additive model data
dataset.summary: Draws from a GAM: a named shape per uniform feature, through a link, with a Gaussian, binomial, Poisson or gamma response.

dataset.name: Anisotropic blobs
dataset.summary: Gaussian blobs sheared by one linear map, so the clusters are elongated (the scikit-learn k-means example).

dataset.name: Uniform annulus
dataset.summary: Points uniform on a shell around the data: out-of-distribution points for density and energy scores.

dataset.name: AR regimes
dataset.summary: A series that switches between autoregressive regimes at changepoints.

dataset.name: AR series
dataset.summary: An autoregressive series started near stationarity (coefficients default [0.8]).

dataset.name: Bars and stripes
dataset.summary: Every bars-and-stripes pattern on a square grid.

dataset.name: Bishop's inverse problem
dataset.summary: t ~ U(0, 1) observed through x = t + 0.3 sin(2πt) + ε; predicting t from x has up to three answers.

dataset.name: Gaussian blobs
dataset.summary: Isotropic Gaussian blobs around random or evenly spaced centres (scikit-learn make_blobs).

dataset.name: Occasionally dishonest casino
dataset.summary: Die rolls from a two-state hidden Markov model: a fair die and a loaded one.

dataset.name: Checkerboard
dataset.summary: Points on a board of alternating tiles, the class given by the tile colour.

dataset.name: Checkerboard image
dataset.summary: A greyscale checkerboard of square tiles.

dataset.name: Concentric circles
dataset.summary: A small circle inside a large one, with Gaussian noise (scikit-learn make_circles).

dataset.name: Click log
dataset.summary: Logged rankings and clicks under a position-bias or cascade click model.

dataset.name: One-dimensional smooth regression
dataset.summary: A smooth curve on [0, 1] with heteroscedastic normal or skewed noise, Poisson counts, Bernoulli outcomes or gamma responses; the truth knows the whole law, so the true expectile curves.

dataset.name: Digit glyphs
dataset.summary: The ten digits of a 5 × 7 pixel font.

dataset.name: Noisy digits
dataset.summary: Copies of the 5 × 7 digit glyphs with flipped pixels and Gaussian noise, labelled by digit.

dataset.name: Floorplan walks (synthetic behaviour)
dataset.summary: Synthetic walks in a house from the sofa to the front door, kitchen, landing or study, branching at doorways.

dataset.name: Friedman #1
dataset.summary: Friedman's first benchmark: a nonlinear function of five uniform inputs plus uninformative ones.

dataset.name: Grid of Gaussians
dataset.summary: Gaussian modes on a square grid (25 by default); exact density.

dataset.name: Ring of Gaussians
dataset.summary: Gaussian modes evenly spaced on a circle, the GAN mode-collapse benchmark; exact density.

dataset.name: Gaussian classes
dataset.summary: Gaussian classes with given means and covariances; separation sets d′, the Mahalanobis distance of the closest means.

dataset.name: Gradient image
dataset.summary: A linear ramp in a direction, or a radial one from the centre.

dataset.name: Interleaved functions
dataset.summary: Two lines that take turns over alternating bands of x.

dataset.name: Linear regression data
dataset.summary: A linear model with Gaussian noise and AR(1)-correlated features.

dataset.name: Mean shifts
dataset.summary: A piecewise-constant mean in Gaussian noise, with changepoints drawn at a constant hazard.

dataset.name: Modular arithmetic
dataset.summary: The table of a ∘ b mod p for +, −, × or ÷, split into train and test pairs by fraction.

dataset.name: Two moons
dataset.summary: Two interleaving half circles with Gaussian noise (scikit-learn make_moons).

dataset.name: Neural ODE failure cases (crossing, splitting, scaling)
dataset.summary: 1-d starts and targets a neural ODE cannot map: swapping places, one start to two targets, spread distances.

dataset.name: Paired shapes (image and caption)
dataset.summary: Coloured shapes seen as a small image and as a noisy attribute caption, paired row by row, with held-out shape–colour combinations.

dataset.name: Piecewise linear
dataset.summary: K lines on consecutive intervals with jumps at known breakpoints; the regime of each row is known.

dataset.name: Pinwheel
dataset.summary: Curved arms turning about the origin, one mode per arm; exact density as an integral along each arm.

dataset.name: Poisson rate shifts
dataset.summary: Counts whose Poisson rate changes between segments.

dataset.name: Quadrant planes
dataset.summary: A different plane (regression) or linear boundary (classification) in each quadrant of the plane.

dataset.name: Random walk
dataset.summary: Cumulative Gaussian steps with an optional drift.

dataset.name: Low-rank ratings
dataset.summary: A partly observed user × item rating matrix from a low-rank taste model, rounded to a 1–5 scale.

dataset.name: One-dimensional regression
dataset.summary: y = f(x) + noise for a named function f of one input.

dataset.name: Mixture of regressions
dataset.summary: K lines chosen by a soft gate over x, so the regimes overlap and y given x is multimodal.

dataset.name: Rings
dataset.summary: Concentric rings of radii 1, 2 and 3 with radial noise.

dataset.name: S-curve
dataset.summary: An S-shaped surface in three dimensions; `t` is the position along the S.

dataset.name: Seasonal series
dataset.summary: Level, trend and harmonic seasonality plus white or AR(1) noise.

dataset.name: Algorithmic sequence tasks
dataset.summary: Copy, reverse, sort, Dyck bracket completion, addition and associative recall as "^ prompt = answer ." strings, split by length.

dataset.name: Shapes image
dataset.summary: A rectangle, a disk, a triangle and a checkerboard patch on a dark background.

dataset.name: Spirals
dataset.summary: Interleaved spiral arms, one class per arm.

dataset.name: Swiss roll
dataset.summary: A rolled-up rectangle in three dimensions; `t` is the position along the roll.

dataset.name: Swiss-roll slice
dataset.summary: The Swiss roll's 2-d cross-section, cut into stretches that serve as modes; exact density.

dataset.name: Two-link arm inverse kinematics
dataset.summary: Joint angles of a planar two-link arm from its hand position; the elbow can bend either way.

dataset.name: Variance shifts
dataset.summary: Gaussian noise whose standard deviation changes between segments.

dataset.name: XOR
dataset.summary: Opposite quadrants share a class: uniform on the square or Gaussian blobs at (±1, ±1).

dataset.name: Zipf catalogue
dataset.summary: Item popularity following a Zipf law, with interactions drawn from it.

dataset.name: Worked-example corpora
dataset.summary: The small corpora the text notes work by hand.

dataset.name: Topic corpus
dataset.summary: Seeded sentences about animals, food, vehicles, colours and places in shared frames, labelled by topic.

dataset.name: Toy corpus
dataset.summary: Seeded sentences about pets, food and weather, with plurals and verb inflections.

distribution.name: Categorical
distribution.summary: One of K categories with probabilities p (a vector, or logits).

categories.label: K
categories.doc: number of categories (the length of p)

distribution.name: Gamma (scale)
distribution.summary: The gamma family parameterised by shape and scale θ = 1/β; its instances are named Gamma.

distribution.name: Independent
distribution.summary: Reinterprets batch axes of a distribution as event axes.

reinterpreted.doc: batch axes moved into the event

distribution.name: Mixture
distribution.summary: A finite mixture of univariate components with given weights.

distribution.name: Multivariate normal
distribution.summary: A normal distribution on ℝᵈ with mean vector μ and a covariance, precision or Cholesky factor.

distribution.name: Pushforward
distribution.summary: A univariate distribution pushed through a many-to-one map, summing over preimages.

distribution.name: Transformed
distribution.summary: A univariate distribution pushed through a monotone bijector, with the change-of-variables density.

environment.name: Bernoulli bandit
environment.summary: Arms paying 1 with their mean probability, else 0 (means default 0.3, 0.5, 0.7).

environment.name: Cliff walking
environment.summary: A start and a goal along the edge of a cliff that sends the agent back to the start at a large cost.

environment.name: Cart-pole
environment.summary: Gymnasium’s CartPole-v1: push a cart left or right to keep its pole up for 500 steps; Euler dynamics with a differentiable model.

environment.name: Inverted pendulum
environment.summary: Gymnasium’s Pendulum-v1: swing a torque-limited rod up and balance it; RK4 dynamics with a differentiable model.

environment.name: FrozenLake
environment.summary: Gymnasium’s FrozenLake: cross the ice to the goal without falling through a hole, on slippery ice or not.

environment.name: Gaussian bandit
environment.summary: Arms paying Gaussian rewards around their means (default 0, 0.5, 1; sd 1).

environment.name: Gridworld
environment.summary: A grid of cells with walls and terminal rewards, where moves slip sideways with probability `noise`.

environment.name: Linear bandit
environment.summary: Arms are feature vectors whose mean reward is linear in an unknown θ* (default θ* = (1, 0.5)).

environment.name: Maze
environment.summary: A maze (start, goal, walls, traps) with optional slip: cell-index observations, four moves, a tabular model.

filter-design.name: Bessel–Thomson
filter-design.summary: A maximally flat group delay (phase-normalised); the gentlest roll-off of the classical families.

cutoff.label: W_n
cutoff.doc: edge, as a fraction of the Nyquist frequency

filter-design.name: Butterworth
filter-design.summary: A maximally flat passband; the edge is the −3 dB point.

cutoff.label: W_n
cutoff.doc: edge, as a fraction of the Nyquist frequency
